ai.title: eval-planner writes results to JSON file
ai.summary: evals/subagents/eval-planner.ts now collects all evaluation results into an array and writes them to eval-planner-results.json after each run. This persists agent output and judging results for later analysis. The script also explicitly logs pros to the console.

eli5.text: If you run the eval-planner evaluation, it now saves a plain JSON file (eval-planner-results.json) next to the code, containing every commit it tested along with the agent's output and the judging results (reasoning, pros, cons, overall score). This means the full run is no longer lost to the console log: developers can open that file later to review, sort, or compare results across multiple runs. The script also prints the "pros" section to the screen during the run, in addition to the existing reasoning, cons, and score output.

ai.title: Move planner files to .agents/planners
ai.summary: Relocated decomposing-planner.ts, implementation-planner.ts, implementation-planner-max.ts, and plan-selector.ts from their respective subdirectories in .agents/ to a unified .agents/planners/ directory. This change consolidates planner logic into a single folder structure. No code modifications were made; files were moved with 100% similarity.

eli5.text: The internal planning helpers that organize how the assistant breaks down and executes coding tasks have been gathered into one shared folder. This affects only the background tooling, so nothing you see changes: your workflows, responses, and model access stay exactly the same. It is a behind-the-scenes reorganization that makes the planning code easier to maintain without altering any behavior.

ai.title: New orchestrator agent with lite sub-agents for complex coding tasks
ai.summary: Added orchestrator agent (anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5) coordinating planning, editing, and reviewing for complex tasks. Orchestrator spawns read-only-commander, researcher-grok-4-fast, decomposing-planner-lite, editor-lite, reviewer-lite, and context-pruner agents. New editor-lite (x-ai/grok-code-fast-1) handles easy coding tasks with full tool access. Added decomposing-planner-lite and implementation-planner-lite variants using claude-sonnet-4.5 and grok-4-fast respectively. Updated read-only-commander-lite and reviewer-lite to use grok-4-fast instead of grok-code-fast-1 and grok-4-fast:free. Reorganized agent files into subdirectories (editor/, planners/, orchestrator/, reviewer/).

eli5.text: The coding assistant can now tackle bigger, multi-step jobs by breaking them into pieces and assigning each piece to a smaller specialist helper, rather than trying to do everything itself. Those specialists handle narrow chores like researching, planning a step, editing code, or reviewing the result, so a complex task gets handed off and coordinated automatically. If you watched it work, you'd see the main assistant pause, spawn one or more of these helpers in turn, collect their output, and then either continue or hand back a finished result. The change is already in place for anyone running this setup.

ai.title: Drop :free suffix from x-ai/grok-4-fast model identifiers
ai.summary: The `:free` suffix is removed from all `x-ai/grok-4-fast` model references across agent definitions and type unions. The `ModelName` union in `agent-definition.ts` now expects the base identifier, and the `agent-builder` prompt guidance is updated to match. This change spans researcher agents, planner spawn lists, and eval harnesses, ensuring consistent model resolution without the deprecated suffix.

eli5.text: The software that picks which AI model to use for different tasks has stopped adding a ':free' label to one of its model names. Anywhere the system referred to 'x-ai/grok-4-fast:free', it now just says 'x-ai/grok-4-fast'. This change affects all the specialized helper agents (like the ones that explore code or read documentation) and the instructions telling the system how to choose models. You wouldn't see a visual difference in the app, but internally the system will now correctly recognize and use the model without the old, deprecated suffix.

ai.title: Update recommended models to Sonnet 4.5 and GLM 4.6
ai.summary: The ModelName union in common/src/templates/initial-agents-dir/types/agent-definition.ts updates recommended model identifiers. anthropic/claude-sonnet-4 changes to anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5, and z-ai/glm-4.5 plus its nitro variant change to z-ai/glm-4.6. This aligns the core type definitions with the current recommended model list.

eli5.text: When you configure an AI assistant, the list of available model options has been updated: the latest versions of Anthropic's Claude and Z.ai's GLM models are now the recommended choices. If you open the model selection menu, you'll see slightly different version numbers listed instead of the earlier ones. This affects anyone setting up or customizing an agent, since the default suggestions point to these newer releases.

ai.title: Orchestrator agent config and eval judge handling
ai.summary: Editor agent switched from openai/gpt-5-chat to anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5. Orchestrator spawnableAgents list updated: researcher-grok-4-fast, decomposing-planner-lite, editor-lite replaced by researcher-file-explorer, researcher-web, researcher-docs, decomposing-planner, editor. Eval judge agent now returns zero-score result object with error message instead of throwing when output is not structured.

eli5.text: If you ran a coding task and the helper that actually edits your files suddenly sounded and acted differently, that's because it switched to a different AI model (Sonnet 4.5). The main coordinator now asks five named research and editing helpers to do the work instead of the three it used before. When the quality-checking step gets an answer it can't read, instead of crashing the run, it now quietly notes the problem and reports a zero score with an error message.

ai.title: evals write dev traces to file
ai.summary: run-git-evals.ts writes per-commit trace JSON when NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT is 'dev'. Guts eval_commit.fileStates and top-level gitDiff before serializing to trace-<sha>.json. Internal evals harness only.

eli5.text: When the internal evaluation system runs in a developer's local environment, it now saves the details of each code change it tests to a file on disk. You would notice this as a new file named trace-<commit-id>.json appearing in the project folder after an eval finishes, containing the results of that specific code evaluation. This only happens during development work, not during normal production usage.
